slot.brief: Sum an arithmetico-geometric series of the form a + (a+d)r + (a+2d)r^2 + ... using the standard shift-and-subtract method

stem: The sum of the infinite series $2+\dfrac{5}{3}+\dfrac{8}{9}+\dfrac{11}{27}+\cdots$ is
working:
$S=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(2+3n)\left(\dfrac13\right)^n=\dfrac{2}{1-1/3}+\dfrac{3(1/3)}{(1-1/3)^2}=3+\dfrac94=\dfrac{21}{4}$.

Independent check: Let k = n−1. Then the sum is Σ(3k+2)/3^k = 3·[x/(1−x)^2] + 2·[1/(1−x)] at x = 1/3 = 21/4.
